source.title: SYMMETRY AND COLORINGS: SOME RESULTS AND OPEN PROBLEMS

accepted.question_text: Let ν(G) denote the minimal number of colors needed to color a group G so that G contains no infinite monochromatic symmetric subset, where a subset A of G is called symmetric if A = gA^{-1}g for some g in G. Determine ν(G) for non-commutative groups, and in particular decide whether ν(F₂) is finite for the free group F₂ on two generators.

evidence.quote: For a group G let ν(G) be the minimal number of colors necessary to color the group G so that G contains no infinite monochromatic symmetric subset.
1.2. Problem ( R.I.Grigorchuk). Investigate the invariant ν(G) for non-commutative groups. In particular, is ν(F2) finite, where F2 is the free group with two generators?

accepted.question_text: Does every finite coloring of an infinite group G contain a monochromatic symmetric subset of arbitrarily large finite size, where symmetry means that A = gA^{-1}g for some g in G?

evidence.quote: we define a subset A of a group G to be symmetric if A = gA− 1g for some g ∈ G.
1.6. Problem ( I.Protasov). Does for every finite coloring of an infinite group G there exist a monochromatic symmetric subset A ⊂ G of arbitrary big finite size?

accepted.question_text: For the integer lattice Zⁿ with n > 3, calculate the numbers χ(Zⁿ) that govern the exact minimal-central-set calculations in this setting, and determine the structure of central sets in Zⁿ.

evidence.quote: In this section given a group G we consider two questions: (1) what is the structure of central subsets of G and (2) what is the minimal size c(G) of a central set in G?
2.4. Problem ( [2]). Calculate the numbers χ(Zn) and investigate the structure of central sets in Zn for n > 3.

accepted.question_text: For a group G and a cardinal κ, let ν(G, κ) be the minimal number of colors needed to color G so that G has no monochromatic symmetric subset of cardinality at least κ. Is it true in ZFC that ν(G, κ) ≥ ℵ₀ for every cardinal κ and every infinite Abelian group G with |G| > κ? Equivalently, must every finite coloring of such a group contain a monochromatic symmetric subset of size at least κ?

evidence.quote: let ν(G, κ) be the minimal cardinal number of colors necessary to colorate the group G so that G would contain no monochromatic symmetric subset of cardinality ≥ κ.
Thus under GCH, ν(G, κ) ≥ ℵ 0 for every cardinal κ and every infinite Abelian group G of size |G| > κ. We do not know if this result is true in ZFC.

accepted.question_text: For every finite group G of odd order and every integer r > 1, must ms(G, r) be strictly larger than 1/r², where ms(G, r) is the normalized largest guaranteed size of a monochromatic symmetric subset in every r-coloring of G?

evidence.quote: For a group G and a number r define M S(G, r) to be the least upper bound of cardinal numbers τ such that for every r-coloring of the group G there exists a monochromatic symmetric subset A ⊂ G of size |A| ≥ τ . For finite groups G it is more preferable to work with the normed value ms(G, r) = M S(G,r) / |G| .
4.3. Question. Is ms(G, r) > 1 / r2 for every group G of odd order and every r > 1?

accepted.question_text: Given any ε > 0 and any integer r > 1, does there exist a finite group G for which ms(G, r) < ε, where ms(G, r) is the normalized largest guaranteed size of a monochromatic symmetric subset in every r-coloring of G?

evidence.quote: For finite groups G it is more preferable to work with the normed value ms(G, r) = M S(G,r) / |G| .
4.4. Question ( [4]). Does for every ε > 0 and r > 1 there exist a finite group G with ms(G, r) < ε?

accepted.question_text: Is there a connected compact group G and an integer r for which ms(G, r) < 1/r², where ms(G, r) is the largest ε such that every measurable r-coloring of G contains a measurable monochromatic symmetric subset of Haar measure at least ε? In particular, what is the exact value of ms(SO(3), 2)?

evidence.quote: for every such a group G and every r ∈ N let ms(G, r) be the least upper bound of ε > 0 such that for every measurable r-coloring of the group G there exists a measurable monochromatic symmetric subset A ⊂ G of measure µ(A) ≥ ε.
5.4. Question ( [5]). Is there a connected compact group G with ms(G, r) < 1 / r2 for some r ∈ N? In particular, what is ms(SO(3), 2) equal to?

accepted.question_text: Let I₂⁺ be the set of orientation-preserving involutive isometries of the n-dimensional sphere Sⁿ. Is ms(Sⁿ, I₂⁺, r) equal to 1/r² for all n, r > 1? Equivalently, does every measurable r-coloring of Sⁿ contain a monochromatic subset of measure at least 1/r² that is symmetric with respect to some line through the center of the sphere?

evidence.quote: Given a measurable subset A ⊂ X and a finite r we define M S(A, S, r) be the least upper bound of ε > 0 such that for every measurable r-coloring of A there exists a measurable monochromatic S-symmetric subset B ⊂ A of measure µ(B) ≥ ε. If 0 < µ(A) < ∞ we let ms(A, S, r) = M S(A,S,r) / µ(A) .

6.3. Question. Is ms(Sn, I + 2 , r) = 1 / r2 for n, r > 1? More precisely, does for every measurable r-coloring of the n-dimensional sphere Sn there exist a monochromatic subset of measure ≥ 1 / r2 , symmetric with respect to some line passing through the center of the sphere?

accepted.question_text: Classify ms(X, r) for compact subsets X of positive Lebesgue measure in Rⁿ when n > 2. In particular, determine ms(X, r) for all regular polyhedra in Rⁿ with n > 2, and compute ms(T, 2) for the regular tetrahedron T in R³, equivalently ms(S₄ × I, 2).

evidence.quote: For every finite r we define ms(X, r) to be the least upper bound of ε > 0 such that for every measurable r-coloring of X there exists a monochromatic subset A ⊂ X of measure µ(A) ≥ ε such that A = g · A for some non-identity element g ∈ G.

7.4. Problem. Classify ms(X, r) for compact subsets X of positive Lebesgue measure in Rn, where n > 2. In particular, calculate ms(X, r) for all regular polyhedra in Rn for n > 2. Calculate ms(T, 2) (or equivalently, ms(S4 × I, 2)) for the regular tetrahedron T in R3.

accepted.question_text: For the discrete interval [n] = {1, ..., n}, let bms([n], r) denote the blurred analogue of the invariant ms([n], r) arising from measurable blurred r-colorings. Compute the values bms([n], r), at least for small n and in the case r = 2.

evidence.quote: Taking this infimum over all measurable blurred r-colorings of X, we obtain the definition of the blurred invariant bms(X, S, r).
8.2. Problem. Calculate the values bms([n], r) (at least for small n and r = 2).

accepted.question_text: Let ms([0, 1], r) be the least upper bound of ε > 0 such that every measurable r-coloring of [0, 1] contains a monochromatic symmetric subset of Lebesgue measure at least ε. Determine the exact value of ms([0, 1], r), at least in the case r = 2.

evidence.quote: this limit is equal to the invariant ms([0, 1], r) defined as the least upper bound of ε > 0 such that for every measurable r-coloring of [0 , 1] there exists a monochromatic symmetric subset A ⊂ [0, 1] of Lebesgue measure λ(A) ≥ ε.
8.3. Problem. Calculate the value ms([0, 1], r) (at least for r = 2).

accepted.question_text: Determine the constant c defined by lim_{r→∞} ms([0, 1], r)·r² = inf_{r∈N} ms([0, 1], r)·r² = c, where 1/2 ≤ c < 5/6.

evidence.quote: (7) lim r→∞ ms([0, 1], r) r2 = inf r∈ N ms([0, 1], r) r2 = c for some constant 1 / 2 ≤ c < 5 / 6 .
8.4. Problem. Calculate the constant c from Theorem 8.1(7).

accepted.question_text: How quickly do the sequences {ms([n], r)}_{n=1}^{∞} and {bms([n], r)}_{n=1}^{∞} converge to their common limit ms([0, 1], r)?

evidence.quote: (1) ms([0, 1], r) = lim n→∞ ms([n], r) = inf n∈ N ms([n], r) for any r ∈ N;
(2) bms([0, 1], r) = lim n→∞ bms([n], r) = inf n∈ N bms([n], r) for any r ∈ N;
8.5. Question. How quickly the sequences {ms([n], r)}∞ n=1 and {bms([n], r)}∞ n=1 converge to their limit ms([0, 1], r)?
